records.label: Gyeongsangdojiriji 114-county population aggregate
records.interval_semantics: The source reports an administrative point estimate (42,221 households; 172,174 men and 182,895 women; total 355,069), not a bounded demographic or Malthusian-equilibrium interval.
pressure_evidence: Kim (2022) analyses 114 county/prefecture household and population entries and reports 355,069 people in the Gyeongsangdojiriji aggregate.

The Korean National Drought Information Center records repeated food stress in the compatible period: rice and barley failure with starvation in 1173, severe Gyeongsang/Jeolla famine in 1359, and a 1360 famine said to have killed half the population of those provinces.
The same official chronology records repeated Gyeongsang drought and complete crop failure in named counties in 1402–1403, demonstrating production pressure but not a stable saturation fraction.
shock_flags: Administrative registers measure observed people, not carrying capacity
Province-wide famine and war-era shocks are not resolved at the 114-county boundary
No independent local-food fraction or equilibrium/saturation interval
records.food_regime: rice and barley mixed farming with other local crops; local-food share is not quantified
records.boundary_description: Historical Gyeongsangdo as represented by 114 counties/prefectures in the 1432 Gyeongsangdojiriji; not equivalent to the modern EU5 Korea region polygon.
records.notes: Strong administrative population and independent drought/famine chronology, but it fails the scale-anchor contract because no saturation interval, local-food share, or >=95% historical-to-EU5 boundary crosswalk is established.

records.label: Jinju-mok entry in the 1432 Gyeongsangdojiriji
records.interval_semantics: Administrative point estimate for Jinju in the source table; no enumeration uncertainty or carrying-capacity interval is supplied.
pressure_evidence: Kim (2022, county table) reports 11,945 people for Jinju and identifies the concentration of people around regional administrative hubs.

The official Korean drought chronology records repeated Gyeongsang famine/drought episodes, including the 1359–1360 famine and 1402–1403 crop failures, but does not resolve them to the Jinju county boundary.
shock_flags: 1432 observation is outside the 1337 point but inside the 1100–1500 research window
Jinju is an administrative centre; urban redistribution and military functions are unresolved
No local saturation interval or local-food fraction
Historical Jinju-mok boundary has not been shown to equal the EU5 location
records.food_regime: rice/barley mixed agriculture and coastal-river food systems; local-food share not quantified
records.boundary_description: Jinju-mok as listed in the 1432 Gyeongsangdojiriji; candidate EU5 location is the modern-named Jinju location.
records.notes: Useful named-county validation case, not a training label. The selector matches one EU5 location by name only; the declared coverage is deliberately zero until historical boundary overlap and saturation evidence are independently documented.

records.label: Gyeongju-bu entry in the 1432 Gyeongsangdojiriji
records.interval_semantics: Administrative point estimate for Gyeongju in the source table; no enumeration uncertainty or carrying-capacity interval is supplied.
pressure_evidence: Kim (2022, county table) reports 12,220 people for Gyeongju and treats the county/prefecture records as administrative population observations.
The official Korean drought chronology records repeated Gyeongsang drought and famine episodes in the compatible period, but supplies no Gyeongju-specific saturation fraction.
shock_flags: 1432 observation is outside the 1337 point but inside the 1100–1500 research window
Gyeongju's former capital/administrative role makes urban and institutional food redistribution unresolved
No local saturation interval or local-food fraction
Historical Gyeongju-bu boundary has not been shown to equal the EU5 location
